how: A member begins the goose and supplies its location while calling for help.
Calls recruit builders and repeatedly ask members to defend the goose.
Members propose a goose design, combine shading plans, enlarge its neck and ask to sign it.
The starter reports the imperfect shape and neighbouring activity as building proceeds.
Coordinates locate the initial build and a proposed pixel design invites improvements rather than binding everyone.

why: No coded canvas reply establishes a bare acceptance without a return request; prank thanks and a conditional help offer do not establish it.

how: Members watch encroachment, request repairs and rally defenders against continuing attacks.
Maintenance is observed, but design-combination requests and relayed instructions do not establish that uninformed keepers erased an agreed change.
A suggestion to convert a design into a script establishes proposed automation, not anyone running machine placements.
The start, location and recruitment appear together, so their within-turn ordering cannot be separated.
A call precedes replies about the emerging shape, but those replies do not identify recruited placers or prove recruitment caused construction.
Reports of the emerging goose precede calls to keep its existing form against encroachment.
Upkeep pressure accompanies a script suggestion, but the record cannot establish a transition to deployed automation.
Posting a pixel design invites further improvements and therefore does not demonstrate that the template settled design disagreement.

why: The coded record does not supply a bare written join answering a canvas call, and silent placing cannot be tested here.

how: Participants propose borders, announce truces and negotiate space with neighbouring works.
Members invoke negotiated boundaries to stop planned attacks and tell placers not to overwrite guest art.
Neighbours offer repair for space, offer mutual defence and thank helpers for protecting their work.
Calls for alliances and a reciprocal defence offer instantiate the small coalition range without demonstrating a council.
A guest asks to occupy the goose neck and a later agreement asks placers to preserve that hosted work.
A participant reports working with negotiators on behalf of neighbouring works and their defenders.

why: Requests for restitution and announcements of agreement do not establish a dispute or disclaimer about who may bind placers.

how: Keeping the goose beside contested neighbours is followed by border and truce negotiations.
A negotiated truce explicitly becomes the reason to abandon an attack plan and preserve agreed territory.
A neighbour offers help for space before the later explicit manpower complaint, so shortage cannot explain every help offer.
Border negotiation is followed by an offer of reciprocal defence, but the offer does not demonstrate that the exchange was carried out.
Attacks accompany alliance proposals and a mutual defence offer, but the coded exchange cannot establish a functioning wider coalition.

why: Neither treaty announcements nor restitution demands establish the bounded transition into disputing or disclaiming representative authority.

how: Members call for erasing or converting rival lettering and report attacking it.
Members taunt a rival, claim comparative success and celebrate converting its lettering.
Participants attribute encroachment and attacks to named neighbouring groups.
School rivalry appears in prank talk and canvas taunts, but these concepts do not date that quarrel before the canvas.

why: The coded record does not establish the antecedent timing of a prior tie invoked in the same turn as an attack.

how: The same participant follows a call to keep the goose going with an admitted attempt to cut rival lettering.
An attack suggestion receives a brief dismissal of its worth, while another caller later retreats without an elaborated account of the norm or cost.
An announced attack plan is explicitly withdrawn because a treaty has been negotiated.
Attacks and later taunts address the same rival, but temporal coexistence does not establish that attacking produced the taunts.
Members describe persistent attackers, insufficient help and a goose they fear losing.
A member proposes relocating the goose under the lettering while the existing position remains contested.
Pressure elicits a relocation proposal, but neither a completed move nor insufficient hands as its demonstrated cause is established.
Participants praise the goose and celebrate the finished image.
Members post a timelapse, announce the final form, mourn the goose and mark the event ending.

why: Final images and praise do not establish adopting a successor project, remaking the work elsewhere or carrying it into the room's institutions.

how: After closure, participants challenge a claim to have drawn a crest and answer with remembered activity on the live canvas.
The final-image post precedes praise, supporting that local sequence without establishing all earlier celebration was caused by completion.
A timelapse precedes a later praise post, and a final image receives praise, so recording need not originate in prior celebration.

why: A record is present, but the concepts do not establish a transition from recording into carrying the effort forward.

how: Participants frame the swapped university rooms and related posts as April Fools play and a meme war.
A moderator limits playful participation by removing a game link revealing its maker's real name and offering restoration with consent or safer hosting.
The goose and the university president become recognisable material for the room's mark and its jokes.

why: One room's headquarters notices cannot test an aggregate frequency or establish the absence of decided organization inside an unread chat.

how: Members object to canvas traffic and dispute its worth, while a moderator removes a duplicate final-image post.
Canvas complaints and duplicate removal are observed, but the coded record does not show that recruitment calls caused a posting rule.
Members request a chat, relay an alternative plan from it and point helpers to headquarters for continuing updates.
Members ask what the goose should look like and explain refreshing the canvas and the meaning of a neighbouring game reference.
A neighbouring participant enters a coexistence exchange and offers to help while asking for the goose template.
Neighbour contact demonstrates the ally-visitor range, not recruitment through viewing the mark, subscriber growth or integration into ordinary room activity.
A participant turns a canvas-associated phrase about buying a girlfriend into a joke about the whole university.
A participant's joke supports local recontextualization, not invention of the phrase or a sustained new running gag.
The opening build call supplies a location before the later loss and relocation discussions.

why: A headquarters link establishes a coordination venue, not that a new collective formed around a canvas mark.

how: A participant explicitly permits goose jokes while rejecting an April sixteenth joke as beyond the acceptable boundary.
The surviving objection establishes a boundary claim, but the removed parent prevents reconstructing the joke or the ensuing response.

why: A company-related cooperation joke does not establish contact with that company or another represented person outside the canvas.

how: A threatened neighbour appeals to unequal space and another participant demands land returned as proof of an apology.

why: A tactical retreat and an offence objection do not establish stress-induced departure or repair of a personal quarrel between members.
Public chat links and relayed plans do not establish concealment from rivals, infiltration or warnings about spies.
A complaint about canvas posts does not establish attacking the room's own mark or recruiting others to destroy it.

how: One participant recalls attacking all night and another tells members to return to study when the event ends.
An end announcement redirects attention back to study, marking release from canvas work rather than a demonstrated scheduling constraint while placing.
Members report apparent server overload and advise refreshing before placing pixels.
A participant explains trouble as suspected canvas-driven server overload without independently establishing the technical cause.

why: Cross-room help and diplomacy do not establish a participant claiming membership in both communities.
